As early as the 1930s, local communities and authorities were campaigning for environmental protection in the Northern Territory. In 1956, the park was officially protected under the name Kakadu. In the 1960s, further areas within the current park boundaries were added. In 1979, Kakadu was granted national park status, placing it under stricter protection. ImageDescription.value:
Kakadu National Park, Northern Territory, Australia
As early as the 1930s, local communities and authorities were campaigning for environmental protection in the Northern Territory. In 1956, the park was officially protected under the name Kakadu. In the 1960s, further areas within the current park boundaries were added. In 1979, Kakadu was granted national park status, placing it under stricter protection. In the 1980s, more intensive coordination efforts began between Aboriginal communities, park management, and scientists, including programs to preserve landscapes, animal species, and cultural sites. In 1991, Kakadu was recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site along with Uluru-Kata Tjuta, which strengthened its international protection.
